title: The Cost page shows the ten costliest tasks and agents with their share of the window, and folds the rest into one line
prompt:
Read web/src/cost.ts (`costView`, its `Row`), web/src/components/cost/CostView.tsx and crates/spawn-cli/src/cost.rs (`/api/cost`, which rows it answers).

The problem. The owner's compute track says a landing should cost visibly less and the owner should watch the figure fall (sync/roadmap-effects.md, "Compute"). The Cost page is where they watch it, and after 73e3596d its 7-day list "is hundreds of flat rows with no top-N or fold" (lead-mac, sync/queue.md 23:45; sync/page-cost-2026-11-11-2336.png). The live `/api/cost?window=7d` (read-only, 2026-11-12) has 252 tasks and 168 agents for $1,785.49. Every one of them is a row, most costly first, and none is folded. The 20 costliest tasks are 39% of the window, and no row says what share of the window it is. The few tasks worth acting on are lost among hundreds of small ones.

Required behaviour.
(a) `costView(answer).tasks` holds the 10 costliest tasks, most costly first. `tasks_more` holds the rest as {count, usd, text}, with text "<n> more tasks · <dollars>" ("1 more task" for one). It is null with 10 or fewer. `agents` and `agents_more` work the same way ("<n> more agents").
(b) Every Row carries `share`, its dollars over the window's: a whole percent ("14%"), "<1%" when it is above zero and under one percent, and null when the window cost nothing priced.
(c) The Cost page shows the ten rows, the fold line and each row's share.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/068.sh. The history is seeded as the store holds it. Tasks are assigned through `spawn_control_record()` and folded. Each worker's model calls are recorded as the Bridge records them (`model.usage`) and priced by the loop's cost step (`spawn_cost_record()`), and `spawn serve` answers. There are thirteen tasks of one mission, T1 to T13, each with its own agent. Task k costs k x $0.30, $27.30 in all.
- (1) Under node, `costView` over `GET /api/cost?window=24h` holds T13 to T4. Its `tasks_more` is {count 3, usd 1.8, text "3 more tasks · $1.80"}, and the agents are the same. Twelve tasks leave "1 more task · $0.90", and ten leave null.
- (2) T13's share is "14%", T4's "4%" and the mission's "100%". $3.90 of $1,000 is "<1%", and a window with $0 total gives null.
It fails with 1 on 101077e2: costView lists all thirteen rows, and there is no `tasks_more` or `share`.

The product reason. The Cost page is the figure the compute track steers by. With the costliest few named and their share stated, the owner sees at a glance where the money goes and which task to question, and the page stays readable as the history grows.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/, web/test/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base, any lint relaxation and any build-time code. The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host. Keep every existing check green and add tests of your own for the new behaviour: web/test tests for (a), (b) and (c) (the fold's edges at 10 and 11 rows, the share's rounding and its <1% and null cases, the page rendering the fold line).
